learnings.question: In the 1880s, which psychologist demonstrated that people forget about 80% of what they learn within 24 hours unless they actively work to recall it?
learnings.learning: Hermann Ebbinghaus proved in the 1880s that we forget about 80% of what we learn within 24 hours unless we actively force ourselves to recall it, which is why spaced repetition beats re-reading.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: What term describes the tendency to forget information as soon as we write it down or save it digitally, because our brains treat the act of storing it externally as permission to stop remembering it?
learnings.learning: Researchers behind the 'Google Effect' paper call it Digital Amnesia: the moment we write something down or put it in our phones, our brains take that as permission to stop remembering it.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: What is the primary purpose of breaking a project into small, iterative cycles called Sprints, as practiced in the Scrum framework?
options: To allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments
To increase the total length of the project
To reduce the number of team members needed
To eliminate the need for a project manager entirely
learnings.learning: Scrum breaks a process into smaller, iterative cycles called Sprints specifically to allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments.

learnings.question: In Scrum's Product Backlog, what standard three-part format is used to write a User Story?
options: As a [role], I need [feature], so that [reason]
learnings.learning: A User Story in the Product Backlog follows the format: 'As a [role], I need [feature], so that [reason].'

learnings.question: In Islamic teaching, worshiping Allah and serving as khalifah (steward) of the Earth are two of three core purposes of human life — what is the third?
options: Achieving personal happiness above all else
Preparing for the eternal Hereafter through accountability for one's actions
learnings.learning: Life's purpose is described as revolving around three roles: worshiping Allah, serving as khalifah (steward) of the Earth, and preparing for the eternal Hereafter through conscious choices and accountability.

learnings.question: What Arabic term refers to a mindful awareness of Allah's presence that builds self-restraint and purifies one's intentions?
learnings.learning: Taqwa is an awareness of Allah's presence that builds self-restraint and purifies intentions, fostered through worship.

learnings.question: In Quran 99:7-8, what does the 'atom's weight' analogy teach about good and evil deeds?
options: Even the smallest deed, good or evil, will be seen and accounted for
Deeds are forgiven if outweighed by good intentions
Only major deeds influence one's final judgment
Only public deeds are recorded for judgment
learnings.learning: Quran 99:7-8 teaches that whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it — no deed, however small, is wasted or ignored.

learnings.question: In PCIe power management, which state represents a device that is fully powered on and actively transmitting data, with no power-saving measures applied?
learnings.learning: L0 is the active state in PCIe power management, where the device is fully operational and actively transmitting data, comparable to a computer fully powered on.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: Which PCIe power state is comparable to a computer being completely shut down, offering the greatest power savings but requiring the longest time to resume activity?
learnings.learning: L2 is the deepest PCIe power state, where the device is almost completely powered down, giving the highest power savings but the longest wake-up time.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, which term refers to the actual, unfolding occurrence of events in a person's life, as opposed to Allah's complete eternal decree of everything that will happen?
learnings.learning: Qada' refers to the actual occurrence of events in life, while Qadr is Allah's complete and eternal plan encompassing everything that will ever happen.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: In the Islamic concept of divine decree, sincere supplication (dua) and one's own actions can change what actually happens in a person's life (Qada') — but what is true of that very change?
options: It was always already known to Allah and encompassed within His eternal decree (Qadr)
It only applies to matters of wealth and health
It happens completely outside of Allah's knowledge
It cancels out a person's prior good deeds
learnings.learning: Dua and actions can change one's Qada', but this change itself was always known to Allah and is part of His Qadr, since He is Al-Alim (All-Knowing).
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: According to a hadith in Jami at-Tirmidhi, what happens to a Muslim who sincerely supplicates (makes dua) to Allah, as long as the request is not sinful or for severing family ties?
options: Allah always grants the exact request without exception
The request is only granted during Ramadan
Allah requires the request to be repeated 100 times for it to be heard
Allah either grants the request or turns away an equivalent amount of evil from them
learnings.learning: A hadith in Jami at-Tirmidhi (3573) states that any Muslim who supplicates to Allah with a permissible request will either have it granted, or have an equivalent amount of evil turned away from them.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: In a Pareto-principle-style word-frequency analysis of the Quran's text, what percentage of the entire text do the 20 most frequently used words actually account for?
learnings.learning: Despite the Pareto principle's 80/20 expectation, the top 20 most frequent words in the Quran only accumulate to about 20.83% of the text.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: What term describes the small diacritical markings placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds and pronunciation?
learnings.learning: Tashkeel are small markings placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate which vowel sound to use, similar to how vowels work in English.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: What was a major reason for analyzing the Quran's original Arabic text rather than an English translation, given that Arabic has roughly how many distinct words compared to the ~170,000 in the Oxford English Dictionary?
options: About 12 million distinct Arabic words (a roughly 71:1 ratio to English)
learnings.learning: There are about 12 million distinct Arabic words compared to 170,000 English words in the Oxford English Dictionary, an approximate 71:1 ratio, which was a reason to analyze the original Arabic text.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python
